q1_issues.issue: "various" is not one of the vague-count phrases the `CardinalityPhrase` lexicon lists (a few / several / a handful / dozens / scores / hundreds / a lot of) and expresses diversity rather than counting things, which is the sole use the instruction set permits for that atom.

q2_gaps: free participial adjunct on a clause ("finished his career **playing** for European teams") — the instruction set covers participles only as post-modifiers of a NOUN (reduced relatives) and links eventualities only via explicit connectives or temporal relations, so no relation is available to tie this adjunct eventuality to the matrix one
the determiner "various" (plurality plus diversity) has no encoding — it is neither a proportion word nor a listed vague-count phrase

affiliation "for" ("play **for** a team" = being on that team) — the for-phrase decision procedure enumerates only benefit / acting-on-someone's-behalf (`Beneficiary`) and ground / prize / exchange (`(For …)`)
notes: `(Patient sk_finish_1 sk_career_1)` and `(Beneficiary sk_play_1 sk_team_1)` are both borderline but defensible under the non-physical-change-of-state and substitution-"for" clauses respectively. `(In sk_play_1 sk_league_1)` correctly avoids `Location` for a non-spatial organizational domain, and the `european_team` genus plus modifier genus follow the part-of-speech test.
